arguments.question: What are the typical characteristics of pulmonary nodules in rheumatoid arthritis, and how do they typically progress over time?

facts.answer_text: In the context of rheumatoid arthritis, pulmonary nodules typically present as small, round, and well-defined opacities on chest X-rays. They can be single or multiple, and they may be scattered throughout the lung fields. Over time, these nodules may progress and increase in size, which can be indicative of the progression of the disease. It is important to note that the presence of pulmonary nodules in rheumatoid arthritis is not always straightforward, and further evaluation and clinical correlation are needed to determine the cause and significance of these findings.
